_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.label: Present continuous
entries.usage: Happening now: -iyor.
entries.example: Şu an geliyorum.

entries.label: Aorist
entries.usage: General truths and habits.
entries.example: Her gün gelirim.

entries.label: Past (-di)
entries.usage: A witnessed finished past.
entries.example: Dün geldim.

entries.label: Evidential (-miş)
entries.usage: Reported / inferred past.
entries.example: Gelmiş.

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: Yarın geleceğim.

entries.label: Ability
entries.usage: can: -ebil.
entries.example: Yüzebilirim.

entries.label: Necessity
entries.usage: must / should: -meli.
entries.example: Gitmeliyim.

entries.label: Conditional
entries.usage: if: -se.
entries.example: Gelsen iyi olur.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: The action done to the subject.
entries.example: Kapı açıldı.

entries.label: Causative
entries.usage: make someone do.
entries.example: Yazdırdım.

entries.label: To be (-im)
entries.usage: Saying what someone is — the 'am/are' ending goes straight onto the word, with no separate verb.
entries.example: Ben öğrenciyim. — I am a student.

entries.label: Yes/no (mı)
entries.usage: Turning a statement into a yes-or-no question — mı comes after the word you are asking about.
entries.example: Sen öğrenci misin? — Are you a student?

entries.point: Var / yok — there is, there isn't
entries.label: Var / yok
entries.usage: Saying something is there or isn't there — and it is also how Turkish says someone has something.
entries.example: Evde süt var. — There is milk at home.

entries.label: Not (değil)
entries.usage: Denying what someone or something is, where there is no action word to make negative.
entries.example: Ben doktor değilim. — I am not a doctor.

entries.label: Present continuous negative (-miyor)
entries.usage: Saying what is not happening right now.
entries.example: Ben kahve içmiyorum. — I am not drinking coffee.

entries.label: Aorist negative
entries.usage: Saying what someone never does, or does not do as a rule.
entries.example: Ben et yemem. — I don't eat meat.

entries.label: Verbal nouns
entries.usage: Talking about an activity itself — swimming, reading — as the thing you like, want or find hard.
entries.example: Yüzmeyi seviyorum. — I love swimming.

entries.label: While (-ken)
entries.usage: Saying that one thing happens during another: while working, while eating.
entries.example: Çalışırken müzik dinlerim. — While working, I listen to music.

entries.label: Subject participle (-en)
entries.usage: Describing someone by what they are doing: the man who is coming, the girl reading a book.
entries.example: Gelen adam babamdır. — The man who is coming is my father.

entries.label: Object participle (-dik)
entries.usage: Describing a thing by what someone does to it: the book that I read, the food you made.
entries.example: Okuduğum kitap çok güzel. — The book that I read is very good.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Passing on what someone else said, heard or thought.
entries.example: Hasta olduğunu söyledi. — He said that he was sick.

entries.label: Converbs (-ip, -erek)
entries.usage: Joining two things the same person did: one and then the other, or one by doing the other.
entries.example: Kahvaltı yapıp evden çıktım. — I had breakfast and left the house.

entries.label: The more (-dikçe)
entries.usage: Saying that the more one thing happens, the more another one follows.
entries.example: Okudukça öğreniyorum. — The more I read, the more I learn.

entries.label: Without (-meden)
entries.usage: Saying someone did one thing without doing another at all.
entries.example: Veda etmeden gitti. — He left without saying goodbye.

entries.label: Reflexive & reciprocal
entries.usage: Doing something to yourself, or two people doing it to each other.
entries.example: Biz üniversitede tanıştık. — We met (each other) at university.

entries.label: Because (-diği için)
entries.usage: Giving the reason something happened.
entries.example: Hasta olduğu için gelmedi. — He didn't come because he was sick.

entries.label: Formal progressive
entries.usage: Saying what is going on in the formal wording of news reports and official notices.
entries.example: Toplantı devam etmektedir. — The meeting is continuing.

entries.label: Pretending (-mış gibi)
entries.usage: Saying someone acted as if something were true when it wasn't.
entries.example: Duymamış gibi yaptı. — He pretended not to have heard.

entries.label: Instead of (-eceğine)
entries.usage: Doing one thing rather than the other one you had in mind.
entries.example: Televizyon izleyeceğine kitap oku. — Instead of watching TV, read a book.

entries.label: Accusative
entries.usage: The specific direct object.
entries.example: Kitabı okudum.

entries.label: Dative
entries.usage: to / toward.
entries.example: Okula gidiyorum.

entries.label: Locative
entries.usage: at / in / on.
entries.example: Evdeyim.

entries.label: Ablative
entries.usage: from.
entries.example: İstanbul'dan geldim.

entries.label: Genitive + possessed
entries.usage: X's Y — the possessive pairing.
entries.example: evin kapısı

entries.label: Possessive suffixes
entries.usage: my/your/his attached to the noun.
entries.example: evim, evin

entries.label: Plural
entries.usage: Noun plural by vowel harmony.
entries.example: evler, kitaplar

entries.label: Demonstratives
entries.usage: Pointing something out: this one next to me, that one further away.
entries.example: Bu bir kitap. — This is a book.

entries.label: Comparatives
entries.usage: Saying one thing is more than another, or the most of all.
entries.example: Bu ev daha büyük. — This house is bigger.

entries.label: ile / için
entries.usage: Saying who or what you did something with, and who or what you did it for.
entries.example: Arkadaşım ile sinemaya gittim. — I went to the cinema with my friend.

entries.label: gibi / kadar
entries.usage: Comparing one thing to another: strong like a lion, as fast as you.
entries.example: O aslan gibi güçlü. — He is as strong as a lion.

entries.label: Before / after
entries.usage: Placing something in time next to something else: after breakfast, before class.
entries.example: Kahvaltıdan sonra yürüyüş yaparım. — After breakfast I take a walk.

entries.label: Question words
entries.usage: Asking what, who, where, when, why or how many.
entries.example: Ne okuyorsun? — What are you reading?
